title: Therapeutic Hypothermia for Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: Clinical Report
authors: AAP Committee on Fetus and Newborn
summary:
This AAP clinical report updates neonatal HIE care. The primary abstract supports cooling eligible infants born at ≥36 weeks within 6 hours for 72 hours, with neuromonitoring, neuroimaging and developmental follow-up.

The retrieved official society summary clarifies selected later-presenting and younger infants and emphasizes coordinated recognition and transfer. This record covers that summary, rather than a full guideline appraisal.
findings: Standard approach: initiate within 6 hours, target 33.5°C and continue 72 hours.
At 35 0/7–35 6/7 weeks, treatment may be considered after family discussion; below 35 weeks it is not recommended.
At 6–24 hours, selected moderate-to-severe HIE cases may be considered after discussing potentially small benefits and risks.
Mild HIE: evidence is insufficient. Avoid hyperthermia even when cooling is unsuitable.
Transport cooling requires strict protocols. Continuous neuromonitoring and access to pediatric neurology are emphasized.
comparator: Clinical-report recommendations; no new randomized comparison.
population: Newborns with suspected moderate-to-severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
shortTitle: AAP neonatal HIE: early recognition and cooling-center transfer
limitations: The complete report was not retrieved: its page presented CAPTCHA. Detailed eligibility scoring, exclusion criteria, adverse-event estimates and underlying trials remain unreviewed; use the receiving center’s protocol.
intervention: Specialist-directed therapeutic hypothermia and coordinated transfer.
whyItMatters: An ED encountering a newborn with suspected HIE should urgently contact a cooling center. Presentation beyond 6 hours should prompt specialist assessment rather than automatic dismissal of possible eligibility.
evidenceNotes: Official AAP News summary retrieved in full: https://publications.aap.org/aapnews/news/34085/AAP-report-provides-update-on-therapeutic . Primary publisher indexed abstract/date and PubMed identifiers corroborated. DOI-specific correction/retraction search found no separate notice; full-report evidence and safety appraisal remains queued.
primaryEndpoint: Prevention of death or moderate-to-severe neurodevelopmental impairment.
guidelineStrength: AAP recommendations; formal GRADE certainty was not established from reviewed material.
